note: Every node and every edge is a field in the register. Nothing here is drawn.

nodes.label: Bret Victor
nodes.principle: Immediate connection between creator and creation — a creator needs to see what they are making, as they make it.

nodes.label: Simon Wardley & Wardley Maps
nodes.principle: Situational awareness before strategy — draw the map before you argue about the move, and the map is a falsifiable claim about position and movement rather than a picture of your opinions.

nodes.label: Tim Berners-Lee & the Semantic Web
nodes.principle: Meaning should be machine-readable, so that independent parties can exchange it without agreeing on a schema first.

nodes.label: Graphs
nodes.principle: Structure is edges. What a thing is matters less than what it connects to, and a model that records connection can answer questions its designer did not anticipate.

nodes.label: OWASP & the security community
nodes.principle: Knowledge compounds fastest in the open, among people who owe each other nothing — and the format of the gathering decides whether it compounds at all.

nodes.label: Flow, and coding in the zone
nodes.principle: Clear goals, immediate feedback and a challenge matched to skill produce the zone — so a methodology's job is to protect those three conditions, not to optimise throughput.

nodes.label: Open source & its licences
nodes.principle: Releasing work is how it compounds — and the licence is the constitution, not the paperwork: it decides who can build on this and what they owe.

nodes.label: Niklas Luhmann & the Zettelkasten
nodes.principle: External memory works as a thinking partner when its units are atomic, uniquely addressed, densely linked and allowed to grow structure rather than being filed into one.

nodes.label: Anders Ericsson & deliberate practice
nodes.principle: Expertise comes from structured practice with immediate feedback at the edge of current ability — not from hours, and not from experience.

nodes.label: Karl Popper & falsifiability
nodes.principle: A claim earns its status by being refutable. If nothing could show it to be wrong, it is not saying anything.

nodes.label: Linus Torvalds
nodes.principle: Tools that decentralise trust change how people are able to work together — and the change comes from the data model, not from the policy on top of it.

nodes.label: Bruce Schneier
nodes.principle: Security failures are usually incentive failures wearing a technical costume — ask who bears the cost of the failure before asking how the failure happens.

nodes.label: Design, with a capital D
nodes.principle: Design is not decoration applied after engineering — it is how the thing works. Start from what the person is trying to do and work backwards to the simplest interaction that does it.

nodes.label: The wider design canon
nodes.principle: Every element must earn its place. Hierarchy, affordance and proportion are properties of any designed thing — an API and a CLI included, not only a screen.

nodes.label: Mihály Csíkszentmihályi
nodes.principle: Optimal experience has measurable preconditions, which means environments can be engineered for it rather than hoped for.

nodes.label: Neil Peart & Rush
nodes.principle: *(hypothesis, not a finding)* Technical mastery in service of meaning — the craftsman-lyricist: virtuosity that exists to say something rather than to be noticed.

nodes.label: Kevin Kelly's books
nodes.principle: *(hypothesis)* Technology is an evolutionary system with its own tendencies — some directions are pushed on us by what has already been built, rather than chosen.

nodes.label: Simon Sinek — the golden circle
nodes.principle: Purpose before mechanism: say why this exists before saying what it does, because the why is what people can act on.

nodes.label: The Cathedral and the Bazaar
nodes.principle: Release early, release often, and let the people using the thing find what is wrong with it — openness as a development method rather than a licensing choice.

nodes.label: David Rice — “Upon the Threshold of Opportunity”
nodes.principle: *(hypothesis)* Security is an economic and societal opportunity rather than a fear industry — the argument of *Geekonomics*, made to a room of practitioners.

nodes.label: Music, and playing in a band
nodes.principle: *(hypothesis)* Playing together in real time is the original experience of collaborative flow — several people, immediate feedback, no possibility of stopping to plan.

nodes.label: Diverse and distributed teams
nodes.principle: *(hypothesis)* Distribution forces thinking to become explicit, written and asynchronous — and cognitive diversity is what stops a team agreeing quickly on the wrong thing.

nodes.label: Christopher Alexander
nodes.principle: Code is a space that people inhabit. A pattern is a named solution to a recurring problem in a context — and a language of patterns is what lets a place be built by many hands and still be coherent.

nodes.label: Team Topologies & Cynefin
nodes.principle: Organisational structure and problem-domain sensemaking are engineering concerns: the shape of the team decides the shape of the system, and the kind of problem decides which practice is appropriate.

nodes.label: Vannevar Bush & the memex
nodes.principle: The mind works by association, and an external memory should too — trails between documents, made by a person and followable by anyone afterwards.
